EngLawName: Regulations of Temporary Entry Permit for Foreigners
name: 外國人臨時入國許可辦法
histories: This entire Act’s 16 articles were promulgated by the Ministry of Interior and went into effect on June 27, 2000.
This entire Act’s 12 articles were amended and promulgated on July 18, 2008 by the Ministry of Interior. The effective date of August 1, 2008 was determined by the Ministry of Interior.
This Act’s article 9 and 12 were amended and promulgated on December 14, 2009 by the Ministry of Interior.
This Act’s article 9 and 12 were amended and promulgated on May 7, 2014 by the Ministry of Interior.
A total of 12 articles were amended and promulgated by the Decree of the Ministry of the Interior Tai-Nei-Yi-Tzu No. 11509326241 on August 20, 2026 and went into effect on the same date.

articles.content: The Regulations are enacted in accordance with Paragraph 2 of Article 19 of the Immi-gration Act (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”).

The Regulations shall apply to foreign nationals arriving by aircraft, vessel, or other means of transportation who apply for temporary entry under any of the circum-stances specified in the subparagraphs of Paragraph 1 of Article 19 of the Act. The same shall apply to applicants who also hold the nationality of the R.O.C. (Taiwan) but apply for temporary entry using a foreign passport, unless otherwise stipulated in other laws and regulations.

Foreign nationals entering the State temporarily shall enter and exit the State after presenting the Temporary Entry Permit for inspection. Foreign nationals who apply for the permit through Subparagraph 2 or 3 of Paragraph 1 of Article 19 of the Act shall be verified at the time of issuing the Temporary Entry Permit or stamping on the name list.
Aircraft captains, vessel captains, or transport operators who have notified the NIA in accordance with Paragraph 2 of Article 49 of the Act shall report directly to the NIA offic-es having jurisdiction over the airport or seaport from which the aircraft, vessel, or other means of transportation departs the State.

Foreign nationals who are granted a Temporary Entry Permit shall comply with the fol-lowing regulations during their period of stay:
1. Foreign nationals applying for temporary entry in accordance with Article 3 of the Regulations may remain in the State until their means of transportation departs the State on the same day or until the day the earliest available means of transpor-tation departs the State. Extensions shall not be granted.
2. Foreign nationals applying for temporary entry in accordance with Subparagraph 2 or 3 of Paragraph 1 of Article 19 of the Act may remain in the State until their de-parture on the same day or until the day on which the earliest available means of transportation departs the State. Upon expiration of the permit, applicants who are unable to depart as scheduled shall apply for a visa in accordance with the ap-plicable regulations.
3. Foreign nationals applying for temporary entry in accordance with Subparagraph 1 of Article 4 of the Regulations may remain in the State until the date of departure of the means of transportation assigned to their duties. Extensions shall not be granted.
4. Foreign nationals applying for temporary entry in accordance with Subparagraph 2 of the Article 4 of the Regulations:
a. In accordance with Paragraph 1 of Article 26 of the Act for Distant Water Fisher-ies, crew members employed overseas may remain in the State for 7 days. Where necessary, one extension of up to 7 days may be granted once. For those who are unable to depart within the permitted period of stay, the captain, transport operators, or their agents shall submit a letter of approval issued by the municipal or county (city) government to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and apply for a visa on their behalf.
b. In cases other than those specified in the preceding item, visitors may be grant-ed temporary stay for 30 days. Where the vessel enters a seaport in the State for repairs, replenishment of supplies, or loading or unloading cargo, and a contin-ued stay is necessary, an application for one additional extension of up to 30 days shall be submitted to the NIA office located near the seaport, together with supporting documents issued by the harbor management authority. If the appli-cant is unable to depart within the permitted period of stay, the transport oper-ators or their agents shall apply to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for a visa to-gether with the supporting documents issued by the harbor management au-thority.
5. Foreign nationals applying for temporary entry in accordance with Subparagraph 3 of Article 4 of the Regulations may be granted a 7-day temporary stay. Where nec-essary, an extension of stay may be requested once; the extended period shall be limited to 30 days. Those who are unable to depart the State within the permitted period shall submit the following documents to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs when applying for a visitor visa.
a. Supporting documents issued upon special review and approval by the NIA.
b. Supporting documents issued by the central competent authority of the industry concerned.
If the date of departure from the State of the earliest available means of transporta-tion or the means of transportation assigned to their duties, as referred to in Subpar-agraphs 1 to 3 of the preceding paragraph, falls more than 7 days after the day fol-lowing the date of entry, the period of temporary stay shall still be limited to 7 days from the day following the date of temporary entry. However, applicants applying for temporary entry in accordance with Subparagraph 4 of Article 3 may not remain in the State for more than 2 days.

Where a vessel captain or transport operator applies for temporary entry on behalf of vessel crew members or service personnel in accordance with Subparagraph 2 or 3 of Article 3, or Subparagraph 3 of Article 4, and any such crew member or personnel violates any of the circumstances in Subparagraphs 3 to 5 of Paragraph 1 of Article 7 of the Regulations, the NIA shall take the following measures:
1. Where a violation has occurred once within one year, the vessel captain or transport operator applying for temporary entry of such personnel for the second time shall be required to employ security personnel to accompany the foreign na-tional concerned.
2. Where 2 violations have occurred within one year, applications for temporary en-try submitted by the vessel captain or transport operator during the same year shall be denied.

Where a foreign national has temporarily entered the State in accordance with Sub-paragraph 2 or 3 of Paragraph 1 of Article 19 of the Act, no application for temporary entry has been submitted, and the foreign national’s country or region of nationality has no embassy, consulate, or authorized representative office in the State, or the foreign national is stateless or of undetermined nationality, and it is established that the foreign national intended to enter the State unlawfully, the NIA shall treat such entry as an entry without permission.
The Regulations shall come into effect on the date of promulgation.
